content:
More and more users are complaining about encountering the spinning rainbow wheel (beach ball) issue when using their Mac on macOS 26.5, with some also reporting that the trackpad becomes completely unresponsive for several seconds at a time.

Activity Monitor typically shows three culprits, and it now appears there is a reliable fix for the issue...

I mentioned this issue last month, speculating at the time that it might be caused by the photo scanning feature of Apple Intelligence. Checking Activity Monitor usually reveals one, two, or three processes consuming extremely high CPU resources.

Michael Simon of Macworld also fell victim to this problem.

He tried many methods without success, and only eventually found one that worked: deleting the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. Doing so means the Mac will of course have to rebuild the Spotlight index, but he said the issue did not reappear even after two weeks. My own usage time has been less than a day, but so far I have not encountered the same problem again.

If you don't mind waiting for the Spotlight data to be rebuilt, you can follow the steps below to delete the data:

  • Open a Finder window
  • In the "Go" menu, select "Go to Folder..."
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Use CMD-A to select all, then right-click on any item and choose "Move to Trash"
  • Right-click on the Trash and select "Empty Trash"
  • Confirm the operation when prompted

If you are also experiencing the same issue, please feel free to let us know in the comments section whether this method works for you.
